subject.title: Aborted heartbeat run floods delivery channel with raw tool output, bypassing ackMaxChars

question: For an aborted heartbeat, should OpenClaw discard all accumulated partial output, or emit one bounded failure/status message before delivery?
rationale: The issue crosses intentional heartbeat alert delivery, partial streaming behavior, and channel safety; source evidence supports the bug report but does not select the user-visible abort contract.

options.title: Drop aborted-run payloads
options.body: Discard all partial/deferred heartbeat output after an abort and record diagnostics only, preventing raw tool output from reaching users.

options.title: Send one bounded status
options.body: Replace aborted partial output with one explicitly bounded failure/status message, preserving visibility without replaying stream chunks.

options.title: Add a general flood guard too
options.body: Pair either policy with a per-target chunk-collapse limit, accepting wider channel-delivery semantics and validation scope.

recommendation.title: Drop aborted-run payloads
recommendation.body: Discard all partial/deferred heartbeat output after an abort and record diagnostics only, preventing raw tool output from reaching users.

likelyOwner.reason: Their directly related heartbeat-delivery proposal exposes the policy boundary that needs an owner decision, although the closed branch is not itself the recommended fix.
